title.it: L'ipotesi nel passato: if I'd known
title.en: If I'd known, I'd have come

goal.sl: Poveš, kaj bi bilo, če bi se takrat zgodilo drugače (If I'd known, I'd have come), ločiš oba 'd in veš, kako ljudje to rečejo.
goal.de: Du sagst, was gewesen wäre, wenn es damals anders gekommen wäre (If I'd known, I'd have come), unterscheidest die beiden 'd und weißt, wie die Leute es sagen.
goal.it: Dici che cosa sarebbe successo se allora fosse andata diversamente (If I'd known, I'd have come), distingui i due 'd e sai come lo dice la gente.
goal.en: You can say what would have been if things had gone differently (If I'd known, I'd have come), tell the two 'd apart and know how people say it.

say.sl: Kar se ni zgodilo in se ne da več spremeniti: **if** + **had** + deležnik, v drugem delu **would have** + deležnik. **If I had known, I would have come.** (Če bi {m:vedel|f:vedela}, bi {m:prišel|f:prišla}.) Nisem vedel{m:|f:a}, nisem {m:prišel|f:prišla}. **If we had left earlier, we would have caught the bus.** (Če bi šli prej, bi ujeli avtobus.)
say.de: Was nicht geschehen ist und sich nicht mehr ändern lässt: **if** + **had** + Partizip, im anderen Teil **would have** + Partizip. **If I had known, I would have come.** (Wenn ich es gewusst hätte, wäre ich gekommen.) Ich wusste es nicht. **If we had left earlier, we would have caught the bus.** (Wenn wir früher gegangen wären, hätten wir den Bus erwischt.)
say.it: Ciò che non è successo e non si può più cambiare: **if** + **had** + participio, **would have** + participio nell'altra parte. **If I had known, I would have come.** (Se l'avessi saputo, sarei venut{m:o|f:a}.) Non lo sapevo. **If we had left earlier, we would have caught the bus.** (Se fossimo partiti prima, avremmo preso l'autobus.)
say.en: What didn't happen and can't change now: **if** + **had** + the participle, **would have** + the participle in the other half. **If I had known, I would have come.** (I didn't know, I didn't come.) **If we had left earlier, we would have caught the bus.** (We missed it.)

examples.en: If I had known, I would have come.
examples.de: Wenn ich es gewusst hätte, wäre ich gekommen.

examples.en: If we had left earlier, we would have caught the bus.
examples.sl: Če bi šli prej, bi ujeli avtobus.
examples.de: Wenn wir früher gegangen wären, hätten wir den Bus erwischt.
examples.it: Se fossimo partiti prima, avremmo preso l'autobus.

ask.prompt: I didn't know the bus was late. If I ___, I'd have walked.

explain.sl:
**Za if: had + deležnik**
- If I had known, I'd have walked.
explain.de:
**Nach if: had + Partizip**
- If I had known, I'd have walked.
explain.it:
**Dopo if: had + participio**

explain.en:
**After if: had + the participle**
- If I had known, I'd have walked.

say.sl: Ljudje dvakrat rečejo **'d**: **If I'd known, I'd have come.** Prvi **'d** je **had**: stoji za if, za njim je deležnik. Drugi **'d** je **would**: za njim je **have**. **If she'd asked, I'd have helped.** (Če bi vprašala, bi {m:pomagal|f:pomagala}.)
say.de: Man sagt zweimal **'d**: **If I'd known, I'd have come.** Das erste **'d** ist **had**: Es steht nach if, danach das Partizip. Das zweite **'d** ist **would**: Danach kommt **have**. **If she'd asked, I'd have helped.** (Wenn sie gefragt hätte, hätte ich geholfen.)
say.it: Si dice due volte **'d**: **If I'd known, I'd have come.** Il primo **'d** è **had**: sta dopo if, poi viene il participio. Il secondo **'d** è **would**: poi viene **have**. **If she'd asked, I'd have helped.** (Se avesse chiesto, avrei aiutato.)
say.en: People say **'d** twice: **If I'd known, I'd have come.** The first **'d** is **had**: it stands after if, the participle follows. The second **'d** is **would**: **have** follows. **If she'd asked, I'd have helped.**

say.sl: Zanikano: **hadn't**, **wouldn't have**. **If it hadn't rained, we wouldn't have stayed.** (Če ne bi deževalo, ne bi ostali.) Drugi del ima tudi **could have** (lahko) in **might have** (morda): **If you'd asked, I could have helped.** (Če bi {m:vprašal|f:vprašala}, bi lahko {m:pomagal|f:pomagala}.) **If we'd run, we might have caught it.** (Če bi tekli, bi ga morda ujeli.)
say.de: Verneint: **hadn't**, **wouldn't have**. **If it hadn't rained, we wouldn't have stayed.** (Wenn es nicht geregnet hätte, wären wir nicht geblieben.) Der andere Teil auch **could have** (hätte können) und **might have** (vielleicht): **If you'd asked, I could have helped.** (Wenn du gefragt hättest, hätte ich helfen können.) **If we'd run, we might have caught it.** (Wenn wir gelaufen wären, hätten wir ihn vielleicht erwischt.)
say.it: Al negativo: **hadn't**, **wouldn't have**. **If it hadn't rained, we wouldn't have stayed.** (Se non avesse piovuto, non saremmo rimasti.) L'altra parte anche **could have** (avrei potuto) e **might have** (forse): **If you'd asked, I could have helped.** (Se avessi chiesto, avrei potuto aiutare.) **If we'd run, we might have caught it.** (Se avessimo corso, forse l'avremmo preso.)
say.en: With not: **hadn't**, **wouldn't have**. **If it hadn't rained, we wouldn't have stayed.** The other half also takes **could have** and **might have**: **If you'd asked, I could have helped.** **If we'd run, we might have caught it.**

say.sl: Kako se reče: **would have** je v govoru **would've**, sliši se kot **woulda**, zato ljudje pišejo tudi *would of*. Marsikdo reče tudi *If I'd have known*, to boš slišal{m:|f:a}. Pisno velja **If I had known**, **would have**.
say.de: Wie man es sagt: **would have** ist gesprochen **would've**, es klingt wie **woulda**, darum schreibt man auch *would of*. Viele sagen auch *If I'd have known*, das wirst du hören. Geschrieben gilt **If I had known**, **would have**.
say.it: Come si dice: **would have** a voce è **would've**, suona come **woulda**, perciò si scrive anche *would of*. Molti dicono anche *If I'd have known*, lo sentirai. Per iscritto vale **If I had known**, **would have**.
say.en: How it's said: **would have** is **would've** in talk, it sounds like **woulda**, so people also write *would of*. Many also say *If I'd have known*, and you'll hear it. Writing wants **If I had known**, **would have**.

say.sl: Primerjaj: **If I knew, I'd tell you.** (zdaj: Če bi {m:vedel|f:vedela}, bi ti {m:povedal|f:povedala}.) **If I'd known, I'd have told you.** (takrat) Slovenščina reče obakrat *če bi {m:vedel|f:vedela}*, angleščina loči: if + preteklik za zdaj, if + **had** za takrat.
say.de: Vergleiche: **If I knew, I'd tell you.** (jetzt: Wenn ich es wüsste, würde ich es dir sagen.) **If I'd known, I'd have told you.** (damals: Wenn ich es gewusst hätte, hätte ich es dir gesagt.) if + Vergangenheit für jetzt, if + **had** für damals.
say.it: Confronta: **If I knew, I'd tell you.** (ora: Se lo sapessi, te lo direi.) **If I'd known, I'd have told you.** (allora: Se l'avessi saputo, te l'avrei detto.) if + il passato per ora, if + **had** per allora.
say.en: Compare: **If I knew, I'd tell you.** (now) **If I'd known, I'd have told you.** (then) if + the past for now, if + **had** for then.

explain.de:
**Jetzt: if + Vergangenheit, would; damals: if + had, would have**

**Ora: if + il passato, would; allora: if + had, would have**

say.sl: Za to, kar bi bilo takrat, je v drugem delu vedno **have**, tudi pri come in go: **She would have come.** (Prišla bi.) **We would have gone.** (Šli bi.) **I would have been late.** ({m:Zamudil|f:Zamudila} bi.) Oblika ostane ista za vse osebe.
say.de: Für das, was damals gewesen wäre, steht im anderen Teil immer **have**, auch bei come und go, wo Deutsch *wäre* sagt: **She would have come.** (Sie wäre gekommen.) **We would have gone.** (Wir wären gegangen.) **I would have been late.** (Ich wäre zu spät gekommen.) Die Form bleibt für alle Personen gleich.
say.it: Per ciò che sarebbe stato allora, nell'altra parte c'è sempre **have**, anche con come e go, dove l'italiano dice *sarei*: **She would have come.** (Sarebbe venuta.) **We would have gone.** (Saremmo andati.) **I would have been late.** (Sarei arrivat{m:o|f:a} in ritardo.) La forma resta uguale per tutte le persone.
say.en: For what would have been, the other half always has **have**, also with come and go: **She would have come.** **We would have gone.** **I would have been late.** The form stays the same for every person.

exercises.text: — We missed the dance! If we ___ (leave) earlier, we ___ (get) there in time. — If your van ___ (not break) down, we'd have been fine! — If you ___ (tell) me the road was closed, I ___ (take) the other road. — Well, if I ___ (know), I'd have told you! — If I'd stayed at home, I ___ (not miss) the soup.

translation.sl: — Ples smo zamudili! Če bi šli prej, bi prišli pravočasno. — Če se ne bi tvoj kombi pokvaril, bi bilo vse v redu! — Če bi mi {m:povedal|f:povedala}, da je cesta zaprta, bi šel po drugi poti. — No, če bi {m:vedel|f:vedela}, bi ti {m:povedal|f:povedala}! — Če bi {m:ostal|f:ostala} doma, ne bi {m:zamudil|f:zamudila} juhe.
translation.de: — Wir haben den Tanz verpasst! Wenn wir früher gegangen wären, wären wir rechtzeitig dort gewesen. — Wenn dein Lieferwagen nicht kaputtgegangen wäre, wäre alles gut gewesen! — Wenn du mir gesagt hättest, dass die Straße gesperrt war, hätte ich den anderen Weg genommen. — Na, wenn ich es gewusst hätte, hätte ich es dir gesagt! — Wenn ich zu Hause geblieben wäre, hätte ich die Suppe nicht verpasst.
translation.it: — Abbiamo perso il ballo! Se fossimo partiti prima, saremmo arrivati in tempo. — Se il tuo furgone non si fosse rotto, sarebbe andato tutto bene! — Se mi avessi detto che la strada era chiusa, avrei preso l'altra via. — Be', se l'avessi saputo, te l'avrei detto! — Se fossi rimast{m:o|f:a} a casa, non mi sarei pers{m:o|f:a} la zuppa.
translation.en: — We missed the dance! If we had left earlier, we would have got there in time. — If your van hadn't broken down, we'd have been fine! — If you had told me the road was closed, I would have taken the other road. — Well, if I had known, I'd have told you! — If I'd stayed at home, I wouldn't have missed the soup.
